cities.name: Cocos Island

places.name: Two Lovers Point / Puntan Dos Amantes
places.note: Cliff park over Tumon Bay, open daily 09:00 to 19:00, and Wanderlog lists admission as free. Good views, but skip it if you have had enough cliffside overlooks by day 5.

places.name: Chamorro Village Night Market
places.note: The Wednesday night market at Chamorro Village, 17:00 to 21:00 and no other night. Go hungry; no prices are posted, so do the Hagåtña sights that afternoon and end here.

places.name: Tumon Bay Beach
places.note: Calm, reef-protected water and the easiest sunset walk you'll do all week, right in front of the hotels. Crowded by day with tour groups but empties out at dusk.

places.name: UnderWater World Guam
places.note: Skip. Small tunnel aquarium, overpriced for what you get, better fish life is a boat ride away at Fish Eye or Cocos.

places.name: GPO (Guam Premier Outlets)
places.note: Standard outlet mall a short drive south of Tumon proper, useful if a typhoon or rain day kills outdoor plans, nothing distinctly Guam about it.

places.name: Micronesia Mall
places.note: Bigger and closer than GPO, has a movie theater and food court, decent fallback for a rain day.

places.name: Proa Restaurant
places.note: Chamorro home cooking, kelaguen and red rice, where locals eat instead of a hotel buffet; short ribs were $15.95 in 2019. Wanderlog now lists it as temporarily closed, so call before you go; 11:00 to 22:00 when open.

places.name: Chamorro BBQ roadside stands (Marine Corps Drive)
places.note: Plate-lunch stands along the main drag, grilled short ribs or chicken kelaguen with rice, cash, no seating to speak of, the $8-10 lunch that keeps a cheap day cheap.

places.name: Alupang Beach Club sunset happy hour
places.note: Beachfront bar with fire dancing shows some nights, touristy but the view over the bay at sunset earns it.

places.name: Ypao Beach Park
places.note: Quieter public stretch of the same bay with shade trees and picnic tables, good for a real swim without stepping over hotel loungers. Free, and the park is open daily 07:00 to 18:00.

places.name: Sandcastle Guam dinner show
places.note: Vegas-style variety show aimed squarely at tour groups, fine if you want a packaged evening, skippable if that's not your thing.

places.name: Tumon Bay reef walk at low tide
places.note: At low tide the reef flat of the Tumon Bay Marine Preserve is knee-deep and walkable from the hotels, with young giant clams and coral recovering from 1990s dredging. Free, an hour; wear water shoes and check tide times first.

places.name: Pleasure Island shopping strip
places.note: The strip of duty-free jewelry and brand shops along San Vitores Road, aimed at Japanese and Korean tour groups, fine for a browse after dinner, not a destination in itself.

places.name: Latte Stone Park
places.note: Eight ancient latte stones with WWII caves behind them, a short walk from Chamorro Village. Thirty minutes is enough, so fold it into the Hagåtña afternoon rather than making a special trip.

places.name: Blue Hole
places.note: A vertical shaft opening in the reef around 80 feet down that drops into open water through a cave, advanced dive site, current and depth make it a poor choice for anyone under 20 logged dives, book through a Tumon shop that runs the Piti sites specifically.

places.name: Fish Eye Marine Park
places.note: Underwater observatory on a pier extending over the reef, an easy way to see fish and coral without getting in the water, worth 40 minutes not a whole afternoon, gets crowded when tour buses arrive.

places.name: Gab Gab Reef
places.note: Shallow calm reef inside the Naval Base beach, good visibility and easy snorkeling, but access requires base clearance arranged in advance through a dive shop, not a walk-up site.

places.name: The Crevice
places.note: A narrow swim-through canyon cut into the reef near Blue Hole, often combined with it on the same two-tank trip, walls covered in soft coral, current can be strong on outgoing tide.

places.name: Piti Bomb Holes Marine Preserve
places.note: Shallow lagoon pocked with WWII-era bomb craters now full of coral heads, good shore snorkeling entry point, free and unguarded so bring your own gear and go at low tide for visibility.

places.name: Shark Pit
places.note: Sloping reef wall named for the occasional whitetip reef shark sighting, not a guaranteed shark dive despite the name, decent coral cover and easier current than Blue Hole.

places.name: Outer Cocos Lagoon reef trips
places.note: Some Tumon shops upsell a combined Piti-plus-Cocos day, skip it, you already have Cocos Island as its own full day on day 6 and stacking both tires people out for no added value.

places.name: Piti Boat Basin
places.note: Small public boat ramp where most Piti dive charters actually depart from, nothing to see beyond the parking and dock but useful to know as the meeting point rather than the dive site coordinates themselves.

places.name: Fish Eye Marine Park Beach Area
places.note: Small stretch of shoreline beside the marine park pier, calm and shallow, an easy add-on for anyone doing the underwater observatory who wants to also get in the water without a boat.

places.name: Micronesian Divers Association (Tumon booking office)
places.note: One of several Tumon-based operators running the Piti sites, book the day before as planned, worth calling around since prices and boat times vary by shop even for the same dive sites.

places.name: Piti Channel
places.note: Deeper channel cut through the reef used as a secondary dive stop when conditions at Blue Hole are too rough, less dramatic topography but more sheltered, a reasonable backup rather than a first choice.

places.name: Asan Reef Flat snorkeling
places.note: Shallow reef flat near the War in the Pacific park, tempting to combine with day 3, skip it as a dedicated stop, the water is often murky close to shore and it competes for time with the actual history site that day.

places.name: Asan Bay Overlook
places.note: Bronze relief maps and a wall naming the dead, above the beach the Marines took on 21 July 1944. Open around the clock, free with free parking; come early, before the heat, when the view down to the reef makes the landing distances real.

places.name: War in the Pacific National Historical Park Visitor Center
places.note: Small NPS visitor center with rangers, a short film and exhibits on the Japanese occupation and the 1944 liberation. Free, no entrance fee and free parking; Tuesday to Saturday 09:00 to 16:00, closed Sunday, Monday, Thanksgiving, Christmas and New Year's Day.

places.name: Asan Beach Invasion Site
places.note: The sand US Marines landed on, 21 July 1944, now a quiet park with picnic shelters and a few rusted amphibious wrecks half buried near the shore. Open around the clock and free, like the rest of the park.

places.name: Ga'an Point
places.note: Two preserved Japanese coastal defense guns still aimed at the reef where American landing craft came in at Agat. Open around the clock and free; small, exposed and shadeless, so pair it with the Agat memorial wall and go early.

places.name: Apaca Point Japanese Gun Position
places.note: A short walk to another set of Japanese defensive guns on Agat Bay, quieter than Ga'an Point and usually empty. Open around the clock and free; only worth adding if you are already looping through Agat.

places.name: Mount Tenjo Overlook
places.note: Unpaved road up to a WWII gun battery site and the best wide view on the island, both coasts visible on a clear day. Rental car needs decent clearance, skip after heavy rain.

places.name: Fonte Plateau Japanese Command Post
places.note: Concrete bunker ruins of a Japanese naval command post in the park's Fonte unit. The grounds are open around the clock and free, but the doors are locked and the interior is not open; access is rough and signage minimal.

places.name: Piti Guns
places.note: Three Japanese coastal defense guns up a short jungle path from the roadside, with a view over Piti Bay at the top. Open around the clock and free; a humid climb, shaded most of the way, 30 minutes.

places.name: War Dog Cemetery
places.note: Small memorial to the Doberman war dogs used by the Marines in the 1944 campaign, with a bronze statue and marker plaques. Genuinely moving in a low key way, not on most itineraries.

places.name: Nimitz Hill Overlook
places.note: Named for Admiral Nimitz's WWII headquarters nearby, but the historic buildings sit on active military land and are not open to the public. The roadside view alone doesn't justify a special trip.

places.name: Agat Unit Memorial Wall
places.note: Simple memorial near Ga'an Point listing units that landed at Agat on July 21, 1944, the second of the two invasion beaches alongside Asan. Pair it with Ga'an Point rather than visiting alone.

places.name: Asan Ridge Trail
places.note: Marked trail climbing from the invasion beach area up into the ridge the Japanese defended, passing foxholes and gun emplacements along the way. Steep, humid, and no shade, go early and bring more water than seems reasonable.

places.name: Fort Soledad
places.note: Restored Spanish fort above Umatac Bay, small and quick, but the view down over the bay and village is the real reason to stop. Listed 07:00 to 19:00 and no fee found, so check the price; no shade, go early before the heat.

places.name: Umatac Bay
places.note: Quiet fishing village where Magellan is said to have landed. There's not much to do here beyond a walk along the water and reading the historical markers, but it grounds the rest of the loop.

places.name: Cetti Bay Overlook
places.note: Roadside pullout with a wide view of the bay and jungle valley below. Nothing to do but look and take a photo, five minutes is enough unless the light is good.

places.name: Talofofo Falls Park
places.note: Privately run park where $22 adults, $15 children covers the round-trip cable car to the falls, a small museum and Yokoi's cave; the price is undated, so check it. Daily 09:00 to 17:00. The falls are modest, the cable car and setting are what you pay for.

places.name: Yokoi's Cave (replica, Talofofo Falls Park)
places.note: Inside Talofofo Falls Park and no charge beyond the park ticket, $22 for adults. It tells the story of Shoichi Yokoi, the Japanese soldier who hid in the jungle until 1972; a 15 minute add-on, daily 09:00 to 17:00, not a stop of its own.

places.name: Merizo Pier
places.note: Small village pier, mostly relevant as the jump-off point for Cocos Island boats. Worth a short stop for the water color and quiet, not a destination on its own.

places.name: Our Lady of Guadalupe Church (Umatac)
places.note: Small village church, simple and not architecturally remarkable, but sits right in the historic core of Umatac and pairs naturally with Fort Soledad.

places.name: Sella Bay Overlook
places.note: Roadside overlook on Route 2 north of Umatac with a view of Sella Bay and an old bridge below. Quick stop on the way south, no facilities.

places.name: Jeff's Pirates Cove
places.note: Roadside restaurant with a pirate theme and ocean view, decent burgers and local plates. Good lunch stop between Talofofo Falls and heading back north, service can be slow.

places.name: Inarajan Natural Pool
places.note: Natural rock pool protected from the open ocean by a reef wall, safe for swimming when the tide is right. Worth a stop if you brought suits, otherwise just look from the rocks.

places.name: Inarajan Village
places.note: Old Spanish-era village core with a handful of restored buildings and a church. Quiet, small, a five to ten minute walk covers it.

places.name: Roadside 'latte stone' quarry markers
places.note: Several small signed pullouts around the south claiming historical or quarry significance. Skip them, they're markers with a paragraph of text and nothing to actually see, not worth burning time on a loop day.

places.name: The Mix (Westin Lobby Lounge)
places.note: The Westin's lobby bar with a casual all-day menu, fine for a first night or a rain day, not a destination. The Island Burger is $20 and the ahi poke $22 on the August 2025 menu, plus 10% service; food 11:00 to 22:00, hours vary, check.

places.name: Tasi Grill (Dusit Thani)
places.note: Dusit Thani's beachfront grill, facing the sunset. The Tasi Burger was $26, fish and chips $22 and the tenderloin $54 on the 2023 dinner menu, so check the price; daily 11:00 to 21:00.

places.name: Alfredo's Steakhouse (Dusit Thani)
places.note: The splurge dinner of the week. On the 2024 menu the fish of the day is $50, the mushroom steak $38, the pork chop $48, lobster $90 and steaks from $68, plus 10% service; daily 17:00 to 21:00.

places.name: Aqua (Dusit Thani buffet)
places.note: Dusit Thani's buffet with theme nights: Thursday Korean, Friday Indian, Saturday smokehouse and seafood, bottomless draft beer with dinner. Dinner $58, daily 17:00 to 21:00; breakfast $37, Sunday brunch $70, plus 10% service.

places.name: Taste (Westin buffet)
places.note: The Westin buffet, dinner Wednesday to Saturday 18:00 to 21:00 only: Wednesday island BBQ and seafood, Thursday South East Asian, Friday and Saturday lobster and crab. $60 midweek, $65 weekends, drinks included; breakfast daily, $38.

places.name: Mosa's Joint
places.note: Modern Chamorro in Hagåtña, a locals' favourite and the 2025 Best of Pacific pick for best off-base restaurant on Guam. Mains run $15 to $30 on an undated listing read in 2026; Monday to Saturday 11:00 to 21:00, closed Sunday.

places.name: Guam Museum
places.note: Opened in November 2016 with 250,000 artifacts; do not miss the Journey of the CHamoru People gallery and the Shoichi Yokoi story. About $3 adults, $1 students per visitors, so check the price; Tuesday to Friday 09:00 to 16:00, Saturday 10:00 to 14:00.
places.neighborhood: Chalan Santo Papa Juan Pablo Dos, Hagåtña

places.name: Plaza de España
places.note: Seat of the Spanish governors from 1736, where Captain McMillin surrendered Guam to Japan on 10 December 1941; see the Chocolate House, the azotea and the three-arch gate. Free and open at all hours, 45 minutes.

places.name: Fort Santa Agueda
places.note: A Spanish hilltop fort from about 1800 with cannons and information panels, and the best view over Hagåtña. Free and open at all hours; 30 minutes, a stop on the Hagåtña Heritage Walking Trail.

places.name: Dulce Nombre de María Cathedral-Basilica
places.note: On the site of the first Catholic mission of 1668 to 1669, with a 17th century statue and stained glass. Free, a $1 donation is welcome; visits Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday 08:00 to 12:00 and 13:30 to 16:30, Mass times differ.

places.name: Gun Beach
places.note: The north end of Tumon Bay, named for the Japanese WWII artillery gun on the shore, with sea turtles and reef fish offshore. Free and no hours posted; the currents can be strong, so swim with care.

places.name: South Pacific Memorial Peace Park
places.note: Site of heavy fighting at the end of WWII on Guam, now honouring Americans, Japanese and civilians, with caves, Japanese graves and the praying-hands monument. Daily 08:00 to 17:00, an hour; check the price.

places.name: Jamaican Grill (Tumon)
places.note: Jerk chicken and ribs on the second floor of the Carlrose Building on San Vitores Road. The combo set with Chamorro rice, salad and mango juice is $31 on an undated voucher listing, so check the price; daily 10:00 to 21:00, hours vary by season.

places.name: Guam National Wildlife Refuge, Ritidian Unit
places.note: A CHamoru village site older than the Spanish by 600 years, with latte sets, cave pictographs and nearly 2 miles of trails. Free, Wednesday to Sunday 07:30 to 16:00, shut on federal holidays and rough-sea days; call (671) 355-5096 to confirm tours.
places.neighborhood: Ritidian Point, Yigo, about 20 km north

places.name: Skinner Plaza Park
places.note: Named for Carlton Skinner, Guam's first civilian governor, with veterans' monuments for WWII, Korea and Vietnam; stop 10 on the Hagåtña Heritage Walking Trail. Free, 20 minutes next to the Guam Museum, no hours posted.

places.name: Chief Kepuha Park
places.note: A small park honouring Chief Kepuha, who let the first Catholic mission in in 1668; stop 14 on the Hagåtña Heritage Walking Trail. No fee or hours listed, 20 minutes on the way to the cathedral.

places.name: Paseo de Susana Park
places.note: A peninsula built from Hagåtña's WWII rubble, with a Statue of Liberty replica the Boy Scouts gave in 1950. No fee or hours listed; walk it before the Wednesday night market next door.

outings.why: Half-day boat trip off Piti with real diving, two-tank dive runs $120–180, snorkel-only cheaper, book through any Tumon dive shop the day before.
outings.name: Blue Hole / Fish Eye Marine Park dive or snorkel
outings.season: year-round, check forecasts July–November for typhoon season

outings.why: The visitor center and overlook are the actual reason to come here beyond the beach, no entry fee.
outings.name: War in the Pacific NHP: Asan Bay Overlook and Ga'an Point

outings.why: Full-day rental car loop through Umatac village and Fort Soledad, the Cetti Bay overlook, and Talofofo Falls Park with its cable car down, 5–6 hours door to door with stops.
outings.name: South loop: Umatac, Fort Soledad, Cetti Bay, Talofofo Falls

outings.why: Short cliffside overlook visit with a small entry fee, skip if you've already seen enough overlooks by then.
outings.name: Two Lovers Point visit

outings.why: Evening market in Hagåtña that I believe still runs Wednesday evenings only, confirm before building the day around it.
outings.name: Chamorro Village night market

outings.why: Full day trip through southern tour operators, boat out with kayak and snorkel included, $70–100.
outings.name: Cocos Island boat, kayak, snorkel package
outings.fallback: Second dive day or just the beach if weather's bad, Guam doesn't punish you for doing nothing.

destination.name: Guam
destination.pitch: A week of warm-water diving and real WWII history off one base in Tumon, not a destination for variety.
destination.caveat: Total door-to-door travel time from most of the US is 18-20+ hours each way, and if you're not a diver the island can start feeling repetitive by day 5. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.food: Chamorro Village night market and roadside BBQ plate lunches.
because.nature: Talofofo Falls, Cetti Bay overlook, and Two Lovers Point cover the island's cliffs and jungle.
because.culture: War in the Pacific National Historical Park is the actual reason to come here beyond the beach.
because.adventure: Blue Hole and Fish Eye Marine Park diving off Piti, plus Cocos Island kayak and snorkel packages.
because.relaxation: Tumon beach at sunset and a slow pace that doesn't punish you for doing nothing.
